title: Body planes, cavities and regions
blurb: Name the plane behind any section, place organs in the correct body cavity, and locate structures by abdominal quadrant, region and regional term.
question: A CT scan shows a slice that separates the patient's upper body from the lower body, and the radiologist notes an enlarged organ in the left upper quadrant. Which plane is the slice, and which organs normally sit in that quadrant?

teach.body: A plane is an imaginary flat surface used to section the body. The sagittal plane is vertical and divides the body into left and right. The frontal (coronal) plane is vertical and divides it into anterior and posterior. The transverse (horizontal) plane divides it into superior and inferior parts, giving a cross-section. Plain English: side from side, front from back, top from bottom.

teach.caption: Midsagittal (median) gives equal left and right halves; parasagittal gives unequal parts.

teach.h: A memory hook for the planes
teach.body: Sagittal splits the Sides, Frontal splits Front from back, and Transverse splits Top from bottom. The midsagittal plane runs exactly down the midline, through the nose and navel, giving two equal halves. Any other sagittal cut is parasagittal. Exam items often describe the cut ('separates the head end from the feet end') rather than naming it, so translate the description into a pair of directions first.

teach.h: Two main cavities and their linings
teach.body: The dorsal cavity holds the brain (cranial cavity) and spinal cord (vertebral cavity), protected by bone and meninges. The ventral cavity holds the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities, separated by the diaphragm. Serous membranes line them: the parietal layer lines the cavity wall, the visceral layer covers the organ, and serous fluid between reduces friction. Examples: pleura, pericardium, peritoneum.

teach.caption: Mediastinum: heart (pericardial cavity), trachea, esophagus, thymus, great vessels. Abdominal: stomach, liver, intestines, spleen, kidneys. Pelvic: bladder, rectum, reproductive organs.
The two lines cross at the umbilicus. Most of the liver is in the RUQ.
Right and left are always the patient's. Epigastric sits above the umbilical region; hypogastric sits below it.

teach.body: Mr. Thompson reports pain low on the right side of his abdomen. His nursing student, Aaliyah, stands facing him, so his right side is on her left. She records it as the right lower quadrant (RLQ), where the appendix and cecum lie, which in the nine-region system is the right iliac (inguinal) region. She uses his right, never her own.

teach.text: Sagittal splits LEFT and RIGHT; frontal (coronal) splits FRONT and BACK. The appendix is in the RLQ, not the LLQ, and the spleen is on the LEFT (LUQ). The lungs sit in the pleural cavities, not the mediastinum.

items: Sagittal = left/right; frontal (coronal) = front/back; transverse = top/bottom.
Dorsal cavity: cranial + vertebral. Ventral: thoracic + abdominopelvic, split by the diaphragm.
Parietal serous membrane lines the wall; visceral covers the organ.
Quadrants: RUQ liver, gallbladder; LUQ stomach, spleen; RLQ appendix; LLQ sigmoid colon.
Nine regions run hypochondriac, epigastric; lumbar, umbilical; iliac, hypogastric.

summary: You can now match any described cut to the sagittal, frontal or transverse plane and place organs in the dorsal or ventral cavities and their subdivisions. You can also locate structures by quadrant, nine-region name and regional term, always from the patient's right and left.

A.q: Which plane divides the body into anterior and posterior portions?
A.why: The frontal (coronal) plane is vertical and separates the front of the body from the back.

whyNot.0: The sagittal plane divides the body into left and right.
whyNot.1: The transverse plane divides the body into superior and inferior parts.
whyNot.3: The midsagittal plane divides the body into equal left and right halves.

A.q: Which organ lies within the dorsal body cavity?
A.why: The dorsal cavity is the cranial cavity (brain) plus the vertebral cavity (spinal cord).

whyNot.1: The heart is in the mediastinum of the thoracic cavity, part of the ventral cavity.
whyNot.2: The kidneys lie toward the back (retroperitoneal), but they are in the abdominal cavity, part of the ventral cavity.
whyNot.3: The bladder is in the pelvic cavity, part of the ventral cavity.

A.q: Which structure separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominopelvic cavity?
A.why: The diaphragm is the dome-shaped muscle that forms the floor of the thoracic cavity.

whyNot.0: The mediastinum is the central region of the thoracic cavity, between the lungs.
whyNot.1: The peritoneum is the serous membrane of the abdominopelvic cavity, not a dividing wall.
whyNot.2: The pericardium is the serous membrane around the heart.

B.q: A CT image shows a cross-section that separates the upper part of the abdomen from the lower part. Which plane produced this image?
B.why: A cross-section divides the body into superior and inferior parts, which is the transverse (horizontal) plane.

whyNot.1: A frontal cut separates front from back.
whyNot.2: A midsagittal cut separates equal left and right halves.
whyNot.3: A parasagittal cut separates unequal left and right parts.

B.q: In which abdominal quadrant is the appendix normally found?
B.why: The appendix and the cecum it hangs from lie in the right lower quadrant.

whyNot.0: The RUQ holds most of the liver and the gallbladder.
whyNot.1: The LLQ holds the sigmoid colon; placing the appendix there is a classic error.
whyNot.3: The LUQ holds the stomach and spleen.

B.q: The layer of serous membrane that covers the outer surface of each lung is the
B.why: Visceral layers cover organs; the visceral pleura covers the lung surface.

whyNot.0: The parietal pleura lines the wall of the thoracic cavity, not the lung itself.
whyNot.1: The parietal pericardium lines the sac around the heart.
whyNot.2: The visceral peritoneum covers abdominal organs, not the lungs.

C.q: Which group of organs is found in the mediastinum?
C.why: The mediastinum holds the heart in its pericardial cavity, plus the trachea, esophagus, thymus and great vessels.

whyNot.0: The lungs sit in the two pleural cavities on either side of the mediastinum.
whyNot.2: The liver, stomach and spleen are in the abdominal cavity, below the diaphragm.
whyNot.3: The kidneys are abdominal, and the bladder and rectum are in the pelvic cavity.

C.q: A nurse checks a pulse in the hollow at the back of the knee. Which regional term names this area?
C.why: Popliteal is the back of the knee.

whyNot.0: Patellar is the front of the knee, over the kneecap.
whyNot.1: Antecubital is the front of the elbow.

C.q: Ms. Nguyen points to pain in the middle of her upper abdomen, just below the sternum and above the navel. In the nine-region system, which region is this?
C.why: The epigastric region is the top center region, above the umbilical region.

whyNot.0: The hypogastric (pubic) region is the bottom center, below the navel.
whyNot.1: The umbilical region is the center region around the navel itself.
whyNot.3: The left hypochondriac region is the top row but on the left side, not the middle.

reteach.title: Slice a gingerbread person
reteach.question: A gingerbread person stands on a table. How would you cut it to get a left and right half, a front and back layer, or a top and bottom piece?

blocks.body: Cut straight down through the nose and belly button: left and right halves, a sagittal cut (midsagittal if exactly centered). Slide the knife flat through the cookie's thickness so the front face peels away from the back: a frontal cut. Chop across the waist: a top piece and a bottom piece, the transverse plane. Name the pieces and the plane names itself.

blocks.text: If the description says 'front and back', the answer is frontal, never sagittal, however many times sagittal is mentioned in the options.

explain.body: Sagittal: left/right (midsagittal = equal halves, parasagittal = unequal). Frontal (coronal): front/back. Transverse: top/bottom.

test.q: A midsagittal plane divides the body into
test.why: The midsagittal (median) plane runs down the exact midline, giving equal left and right halves.

whyNot.1: Unequal left and right parts come from a parasagittal plane.
whyNot.2: Anterior and posterior parts come from a frontal plane.
whyNot.3: Superior and inferior parts come from a transverse plane.

explain.body: Dorsal = cranial + vertebral. Ventral = thoracic (pleural cavities + mediastinum) + abdominopelvic. The diaphragm divides the ventral cavity.

test.q: The cranial cavity and the vertebral cavity together form the
test.why: The dorsal cavity is made of the cranial cavity (brain) and the vertebral cavity (spinal cord).

whyNot.0: The ventral cavity is made of the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities.
whyNot.1: The thoracic cavity is part of the ventral cavity and holds the heart and lungs.
whyNot.3: The pelvic cavity is the lower part of the abdominopelvic cavity.

explain.body: Two layers with serous fluid between: parietal lines the cavity wall, visceral covers the organ. Pleura (lungs), pericardium (heart), peritoneum (abdomen).

test.q: In the abdomen, the serous layer that lines the inner surface of the abdominal wall is the
test.why: The parietal layer lines the cavity wall; in the abdomen that membrane is the peritoneum.

whyNot.0: The visceral peritoneum covers the abdominal organs, not the wall.
whyNot.2: The parietal pleura lines the thoracic wall, around the lungs.
whyNot.3: The visceral pericardium covers the heart.

explain.body: Lines through the umbilicus make four quadrants: RUQ, LUQ, RLQ, LLQ. Right and left are always the patient's, so facing a patient, their right is on your left.

test.q: Facing a patient, a nurse sees a scar below the navel on the side that is to the nurse's left. Which quadrant is the scar in?
test.why: When facing a patient, the nurse's left is the patient's right, and below the navel is lower: the RLQ.

whyNot.0: This uses the nurse's left instead of the patient's; the patient's side is what counts.
whyNot.2: The scar is below the navel, so it is in a lower quadrant, and it is on the patient's right.
whyNot.3: The side is right, but the scar is below the navel, so it is not an upper quadrant.
